title: The end-to-end suite runs on the factory pack alone and proves a rule change ships from this repo

story.i_want_to: have mix e2e drive its sandbox sessions with only the factory pack installed, and prove a policy change end to end
story.so_that: PRD R10's done test holds: a factory feature is built, reviewed, tested end to end and released from the loopctl repo alone

rationale: PRD R10 is done when a factory feature like loopctl#1065 plus #1067 (a server change and the client hook that broke against it) can be built, tested end to end and released from this repo alone. PRD R7 assigns no named path to this release, so this story adds the paths R10's done test needs: the sandbox sessions run on the pack with no claude-config file, a policy edit reaches the hook that enforces it, and the review count survives a move between machines, which the cloud test (R3) requires of every factory state.

acceptance_criteria.description: mix e2e starts each sandbox session with a CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR that holds only the factory pack installed from the checkout's .claude-plugin/marketplace.json and the loopctl MCP server, and fails before the first scenario, naming the file, when that dir holds a file from claude-config.
The happy-path scenario of release 2 passes unchanged on that config dir.

Scenario policy_change_ships, against loopctl.com: the suite reads factory_policy from loopctl.com and policy.json from the pack installed out of its own checkout, first asserts that both carry the version of the checkout's factory/policy.toml (failing with both versions named when the deployed server is at another commit), then asserts that every key of the checkout's policy.toml has the same value in factory_policy and in policy.json (failing with the key and the three values named, so a value edited without a version bump, or a stale server value under an equal version, fails), then, for each key whose value differs between the previous release tag's factory/policy.toml and the checkout's, asserts that the server and the pack carry the new value and names the key in the run report (a release that changed no key reports 'no rule changed' and the run still passes), then opens review rounds on one sandbox branch until the round past review_rounds.code.ceiling is refused 409 review_ceiling_reached with US-52.53's ceiling message; no server is built for the test.

Scenario review_count_moves: a review round counted by a holder on one host, then the item moved to a holder on a second host (move verb, release 7), makes the second holder's next review_round_open answer round 2.

Scenario previous_pack: the happy path passes with the previous release's pack (the version the prior manifest names) against this release's server, so a machine not yet synced keeps working (PRD R7).
After every scenario the suite asserts that no sandbox session wrote outside its worktree, its git dir and its CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, and that the config dir holds no review-round state file.
Each e2e run report names the factory pack version and the policy version it ran, read from the installed plugin.json and from factory_policy.

test_cases.name: a stray claude-config file stops the suite (unit on E2E.ConfigDir)
preconditions: a tmp config dir with the pack installed plus hooks/block-complex-bash.sh copied in

test_cases.name: happy path on the pack alone (e2e, mix e2e --only happy_path against the sandbox repo)
preconditions: the sandbox repo mkreyman/loopctl-e2e-sandbox and loopctl.com at this release's deploy
expected_results: pass; the report names the pack version and the policy version

test_cases.name: policy_change_ships (e2e)
preconditions: loopctl.com deployed from the commit under test; the pack installed from that commit
expected_results: factory_policy and the installed pack's policy.json both carry factory/policy.toml's version and every one of its values
each key changed since the previous release tag is named in the report with its new value on both sides
the round past the code ceiling is refused with 409 review_ceiling_reached and US-52.53's ceiling message

test_cases.name: review_count_moves across two hosts (e2e)
preconditions: the sandbox's two fleet runner hosts (US-52.9, e2e/config/sandbox.exs), each with the pack, a holder (release 3) and the host daemon (release 7)
expected_results: the second host's holder's next review_round_open answers round 2

test_cases.name: previous_pack against this server (e2e)
preconditions: the previous manifest's pack tag fetched into a second config dir
expected_results: the happy path passes with the previous release's pack against this release's server

test_cases.name: write-scope check catches a stray file (unit on E2E.WriteScope)
preconditions: a fake session run that writes ~/.claude/plugins/data/review-round-counter/store.json

technical_notes: The suite, its sandbox repo, mix e2e and its nightly run come from release 2 (README names table: end-to-end suite); this story adds scenarios under e2e/scenarios/ and two helpers, E2E.ConfigDir and E2E.WriteScope, in e2e/support/.

Pack install in the suite: claude plugin marketplace add <checkout> then claude plugin install loopctl-factory@loopctl-factory and review-round-counter@loopctl-factory with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR set to a fresh tmp dir per session; the built pack and marketplace come from US-52.52.

policy_change_ships runs against loopctl.com like every scenario (US-52.9; README names table: end-to-end suite). The policy.toml it compares with is the one in the checkout the run starts from, and its first assertion is that the deployed factory_policy carries that version, so a run at the wrong commit fails naming both versions instead of passing on a stale rule; the scenario proves a rule decided in this repo reached both the server (US-52.51) and the pack (US-52.52) without a second build. The changed keys are read from the last release tag's factory/policy.toml (the tag previous_pack reads); a key absent at that tag counts as changed. No fixture policy is used: a value written only for the test could not reach loopctl.com.
review_count_moves uses the move verb (POST /api/v1/stories/:id/move, release 7, README names table) and the review-round routes of US-52.53.

previous_pack: the previous manifest is read from the last release tag's release/manifest.toml; the pack is the marketplace at that tag. The first time this runs, the previous release predates the pack: the scenario is skipped with the reason 'no pack in the previous release' and starts asserting from release 9 on.

Write scope: the suite runs each session with HOME set to a per-session tmp dir and diffs it after the scenario; the review-counter's old store lived under the plugin data dir, which is why AC-52.55.6 names it.
Release 8 adds these e2e paths although PRD R7's list names none for it; recorded in the release's README section.
non_goals: The happy path itself and the sandbox repo: release 2 (README names table: end-to-end suite).
Running the suite in a Claude cloud session: PRD non-goals; the write-scope check is what keeps that possible.

failure_modes.partition: n/a: the suite runs against loopctl.com and reads it only through its API (US-52.9); loopctl unreachable mid-run is release 10's scenario.
failure_modes.state: AC-52.55.6: the suite proves sessions hold no factory state outside their worktree, so the review count and every rule value live in loopctl and the pack only.
failure_modes.retry: AC-52.55.4: a review round counted before a move is counted once after it, because the count is the item's events, not the session's.
failure_modes.slow: AC-52.55.2: scenarios run under release 2's per-scenario bound of the suite, so a hung session fails its scenario rather than the night.
failure_modes.reach: AC-52.55.4: the second holder reaches the item's review count through loopctl by the item, on another host, without knowing the first holder.

defaults: previous_pack is skipped, with its reason in the report, until a previous release carries a pack.
definition_of_done: The nightly e2e run after the epic merges reports policy_change_ships, review_count_moves and happy_path passed, with the pack version and policy version printed.
